chat.template.none_body: Try another word, or type your question in words.
chat.template.error_title: The templates could not be loaded
chat.template.error_body: The connection dropped or the service is unavailable. You can still type your question.
conversations.delete.running: A question is being answered: deleting stops it, and its answer is not kept.
draft.list_failed: This conversation's drafts couldn't be loaded. {reason}
draft.meta.new: Only you can see it, here. No version of it is in the dashboard list yet.
draft.meta.saved: It comes from a dashboard in the list. Saving adds a new version to that dashboard.
draft.viewer: Only editors and admins can save drafts to the dashboard list. You can look at this one here.
draft.reader: This draft is in a conversation another member shared. You can only look at it: it can't be saved or changed here, and its data is queried with your own permissions, so you may see less than its owner does.
draft.saved.title: Saved as version {version} in the dashboard list
draft.saved.body: Everyone in your organization with access can see it now.
draft.preview_note: Draft preview: the data is queried live, and what you see is what the saved dashboard shows.
draft.saved_changed_hint: If you just saved this version, version {latest} of the saved dashboard is it.
answer_draft.unreadable: A dashboard this answer wrote can't be shown. {reason}
member.last_admin: An organization needs at least one administrator. Make another member an administrator first, then change this member.
member.already_member: This email is already a member.
member.quota_full: Your plan's member limit is reached, counting invitations that are still waiting. Existing members are not affected.
invitation.account_mismatch: This invitation was not sent to this account.
members.title: Members
members.description: Invite colleagues to {tenant} and decide what each person can do.
members.quota.label: Members ({plan} plan)
members.quota.note: Seats include invitations that are still waiting.
members.quota_full.title: The {plan} plan's member limit is reached ({used} / {limit})
members.quota_full.body: Existing members keep working; you just can't add more. A higher plan raises the limit.
members.card.title: Members
members.card.caption: Members of {tenant}
members.empty.title: You're the only one in this organization
members.empty.body: Invite the people who work on the floor or in quality control, and they can see device data and ask the assistant. You can start with Viewer and change it later.
members.invitations.title: Pending invitations
members.invitations.description: The person accepts by signing in with this email; only then do they become a member. An invitation expires after 7 days.
members.help.title: What each role can do
members.help.last_admin: An organization always keeps at least one administrator.
members.role.label: Role
members.role.viewer_summary: Can see devices, data and dashboards, and use the assistant. Can't change settings.
members.role.editor_summary: Can also add and change devices, models, dashboards and alert rules.
members.role.admin_summary: Can also manage members, bind gateways and see the plan.
members.denied.title: Only administrators can manage members
members.denied.body: Your role in {tenant} is {role}. To invite colleagues or change roles, ask an administrator of the organization.
members.denied.body_admins: Your role in {tenant} is {role}. To invite colleagues or change roles, ask an administrator of the organization: {admins}.
members.invite.title: Invite a member
members.invite.description: They get an invitation by email. They join the organization after they sign in to TrustIoT with that email and accept.
members.role_dialog.title: Change {name}'s role
members.role_dialog.description: The change applies at once: the new role is used from their next request.
members.role_dialog.self_title: You will lose the right to manage members
members.role_dialog.self_body: After you lower your own role, only another administrator can change it back.
members.role_dialog.failed: The role could not be changed
members.remove.title: Remove {name} from {tenant}?
members.remove.body: {name} loses access to this organization at once; a signed-in session is refused from the next request. What they created (devices, dashboards, alert rules) stays. To join again they need a new invitation.
members.toast.invited_body: They appear in the member list once they accept.
members.toast.resent_body: The invitation is valid for another 7 days.
members.toast.revoked_body: The link in that email no longer works, and the seat is free again.
members.toast.role_changed_body: The new role applies from their next request.
members.toast.removed_body: They no longer have access to this organization.
members.accept.title: Join {tenant}
members.accept.invalid.title: This invitation can't be used
members.accept.invalid.body: It may have expired, been revoked, or been accepted already. If you haven't joined yet, ask the person who invited you to send it again.
members.accept.mismatch.title: This invitation wasn't sent to this account
members.accept.mismatch.body: You're signed in as {email}. An invitation can only be accepted with the email it was sent to: sign out, sign in with that address, then open the link in the invitation email again.
members.accept.mismatch.sign_out: Sign out and use another account
members.accept.joined.title: You joined {tenant}
members.accept.joined.body: The invitation is accepted, but the page couldn't open the organization. Go to the home page to continue.
alerts.title: Alerts and notifications
alerts.description: When a rule fires the notification appears here, and goes out by email or webhook as the rule says.
alerts.needs_editor: Disabling and pausing rules needs the editor role or above.
alerts.error.title: Alerts can't be loaded right now
alerts.error.body: Rules keep running, and email and webhooks are still sent; this page shows the notifications of the meantime once it is back.
alerts.failure.syntax: The script has a syntax error
alerts.failure.execution: The script failed when run on the data
alerts.failure.trigger_count: It fired too often on the past data
alerts.failure.expected_case: The case that should fire did not
alerts.strip.label: AI rules
alerts.strip.explain: The AI checks your data every day and writes and adjusts rules; a rule that passes its backtest starts at once. You can disable one rule at any time, or pause them all.
alerts.strip.explain_viewer: The AI checks your data every day and writes and adjusts rules. Disabling or pausing rules needs the editor role or above.
alerts.pause.title: Pause all AI rules?
alerts.pause.body: AI-made rules ({ai}) stop judging and notifying at once, until someone resumes them, and the AI will not create or change rules. Member-made rules ({member}) keep running. Data from the pause is not replayed into notifications.
alerts.paused.title: All AI rules are paused
alerts.paused.effect: AI rules ({ai}) do not judge or notify and the AI will not create or change rules; member-made rules ({member}) keep running.
alerts.disable.title: Disable "{rule}"?
alerts.disable.body: After this the rule no longer judges or notifies. Its versions are kept and you can enable it again; the AI will not create the same rule again.
alerts.disable.from_email: You came here from the link in a notification email. The link only leads to this page; the rule is disabled only when you press the button here.
alerts.disable.reason_placeholder: For example: the pressure always dips at shift change
alerts.disable.reason_hint: The reason is given to the AI as input for its next adjustment of rules.
ask.alert.suggest_rules: Ask AI to suggest alert rules
alerts.notifications.more: More actions for the notification of {rule}
alerts.notifications.limit: "{rule}" has notified {count} times this hour, which is its limit; triggers before {until} are not notified, and are still recorded on the rule's page.
alerts.notifications.empty.title: No notifications yet
alerts.notifications.empty.body: The AI checks your device data every day and creates a rule when it sees a pattern worth watching. When a rule fires, its notification appears here. A newly connected device usually needs a few days of data first.
alerts.notifications.none_unread.title: No unread notifications
alerts.notifications.none_unread.body: You have seen everything so far.
alerts.notifications.no_match.title: No notification matches
alerts.notifications.no_match.body: Nothing fits the device and rule you chose.
alerts.rules.caption: Alert rules, {count}
alerts.rules.failed_note: A rule whose backtest failed is not active; only the record stays, so you can see what the AI tried.
alerts.rules.empty.title: No rules yet
alerts.rules.empty.body: The AI writes alert rules from your device data and turns them on once they pass a backtest on the past 14 days. Ask it to suggest some to start with.
alerts.rules.no_match.title: No rule matches
alerts.rules.no_match.body: Change the filters or the search.
alerts.rule.not_found.title: Rule not found
alerts.rule.not_found.body: The rule does not exist, or the link is wrong.
alerts.backtest.title: Backtest result
alerts.backtest.window: Before v{version} started, it was replayed on the 14 days from {from} to {to}
alerts.backtest.cases: {fired} of {total} cases that should fire did: {details}
alerts.backtest.cases_none: It has no case that should fire
alerts.backtest.short_history: The devices have only {days} days of history, so synthetic stretches were added for the cases that should fire.
alerts.backtest.chart_none: No trigger on any of the 14 days.
alerts.backtest.show_table: View each trigger as a table
alerts.versions.title: Version history
alerts.notification_missing.title: Notification not found
alerts.notification_missing.body: The notification does not exist, or it is older than the notifications kept.
alerts.starter.title: Alerts are a Business plan feature
alerts.starter.body: After an upgrade the AI creates alert rules from your device data and tells you when they fire through the notification center, email or webhook; a false alarm can be switched off in one click.
ask.alert.first_unusual: Ask AI what looks unusual first
alerts.starter.note_admin: Only organization admins can upgrade, and you are one. The page to change the plan is not available yet.
alerts.starter.note_member: Only organization admins can upgrade; ask one of them.
alerts.notification_missing.load_failed: The notification this link names can't be loaded: {reason}
documents.title: Documents
documents.description: Upload the manufacturer's manuals and fault-code tables by device model. Once processed, the AI reads these pages when it answers, and names the file and page so you can check the source.
documents.description_viewer: You can read the documents here.
documents.readonly.title: You're a viewer, so this page is read-only
documents.readonly.body: Uploading and deleting documents needs the editor role or above.
documents.unavailable.title: The document library is temporarily unavailable
documents.unavailable.body: Your uploaded documents aren't lost. Until it is back, the AI skips documents when it answers and says so in the answer.
documents.starter.title: The document library is part of Business plans and above
documents.starter.body: Once your plan includes it, you can upload equipment manuals; the AI reads them when it answers fault questions and cites the page.
documents.empty.title: Upload your first manual
documents.empty.body: Put your equipment's manuals and fault-code tables (PDF) here. When the AI answers questions about faults and settings it reads these pages and names the file and page, so you can check the source.
documents.empty.body_viewer: No documents have been uploaded yet. Ask an editor or admin to upload the equipment's manuals and fault-code tables.
documents.empty.models: Documents are sorted by device model. No model yet?
documents.no_match.title: No document matches
documents.no_match.body: Try another word, or clear the filters.
documents.caption: Documents, {count} shown
documents.search.label: Search document names
documents.usage.label: Document library capacity
documents.status.processing_note: The AI cites it only when this is done
documents.status.ready: Done, the AI can cite it
documents.failure.others_ready: The other {count} pages can already be cited.
knowledge.page_render_failed: Page {page} couldn't be turned into an image (the file may be damaged).
documents.background.label: Uploads in progress
documents.background.title: Uploading in the background
documents.message.retried: Processing of “{name}” will be tried again.
documents.message.deleted: Deleted “{name}”. The AI no longer cites it.
documents.delete.title: Delete “{name}”?
documents.delete.body_versions: Every version (up to v{version}), the page images and the index are deleted together, and the AI stops citing the document.
documents.delete.body_citations: In past conversations its citations will read “document deleted” and can't be opened. This can't be undone.
documents.upload.title: Upload PDF
documents.upload.description: Only PDF files are accepted. The AI reads the pages once they are processed.
documents.upload.model_hint: The AI reads these documents only when a question is about a device of this model.
documents.upload.no_models: There is no device model yet. Add a device first, then upload its documents.
documents.upload.one_file: A new version is one file, so only the first file was taken.
documents.upload.not_pdf: Not a PDF. The library only takes PDF files; attach photos to a conversation so the AI can look at them.
documents.upload.over_capacity_refused: Over your plan's document capacity, so it wasn't uploaded. The documents you already have work as before.
documents.upload.as_version: Upload as new version v{version} (the AI reads v{version}; the old version is kept)
documents.viewer.not_found.title: This document wasn't found
documents.viewer.not_found.body: The link may be wrong, or the document doesn't belong to this organization.
documents.viewer.deleted.title: This document was deleted
documents.viewer.deleted.body: This document was deleted on {time}, and the AI no longer cites it.
documents.viewer.no_versions: This document has no version to show.
documents.viewer.old.title: You're looking at v{version}
documents.viewer.old.body: The current version is v{latest}, and page numbers may differ.
documents.viewer.no_pages.title: The pages aren't ready yet
documents.viewer.no_pages.body: The page images appear once the pages are counted and turned into images.
documents.viewer.image_failed: The image of page {page} couldn't be loaded.
documents.viewer.page_alt_cited: The page image of page {page}. The marked area is the part the AI cited, in the {position} of the page.
documents.viewer.aside.title: About this page
documents.viewer.aside.cited_body: The AI cited this page. The marked area is the part it read, so you can check it against the original.
documents.viewer.aside.no_text: A page image has no readable text. For the text, download the original PDF.
